rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated that no image was available to it and therefore did not fabricate specific embryo morphology. It only made general comments about typical Day 4 embryos, which are broadly accurate.
It integrated most relevant factors well, including age, tubal factor, ovarian reserve proxy, sperm quality, endometrium, prior ectopic/miscarriage, BMI, and lifestyle, and linked these to prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with probability ranges tied to assumed embryo quality. Minor issues include some overinterpretation of FSH/oocyte quality and broad assumptions due to missing morphology.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based, but recommending PGT-A strongly in a 32-year-old after a single clinical miscarriage and suggesting immunologic/thrombophilia/NK-cell workup are not strongly guideline-supported in this scenario.

The response gives clear practical next steps for transfer support, counseling, uterine evaluation, and future planning. Some recommendations are somewhat generic or overreaching, but overall clinically useful.
